q: Which furniture is ideal for both seating and sleeping?
n: A futon is a padded mattress on a convertible frame that folds into a sofa for sitting and flattens into a bed for sleeping. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furniture); Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design.

q: Where is a credenza table most ideally placed in a home?
n: A credenza (sideboard) is a low storage cabinet for serving pieces and tableware. Its natural place is the dining room, along a wall. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furniture Types); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: Which structural element is primarily used to resist lateral forces such as wind or seismic loads in high-rise buildings?
n: Shear walls are stiff structural walls that resist lateral wind and seismic forces in their plane. They are the primary lateral system in many high-rises. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (Bearing Wall and Dual Systems); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: Which structural design method is considered the most comprehensive due to its use of multiple load and resistance factors?
n: Load and Resistance Factor Design applies separate load factors to each load type and resistance factors to member strengths. That makes it more comprehensive than single-safety-factor ASD. Source: NSCP 2015, Ch. 5 (Steel – LRFD and ASD); AISC 360.

q: Which of the following software is primarily used for structural analysis and design?
n: STAAD.Pro is software for structural analysis and design. Revit is BIM modeling software, and InfraWorks is for infrastructure planning. Source: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro product documentation; Autodesk product documentation.

q: What is the typical wind exposure category for residential areas with buildings and trees nearby?
n: Exposure B covers urban and suburban areas, and wooded terrain, with many closely spaced obstructions the size of single-family dwellings or larger. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 207A.7.3 (Exposure Categories).

q: What is the minimum parking slot dimension for a parallel parking slot?
n: The NBC sets parallel parking slots at 2.15 m × 6.00 m, which is about 7.05 ft × 19.69 ft. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking slot dimensions).

q: Which of the following best describes a positive latching mechanism?
o: a soft-close mechanism for drawers and cabinets
a magnetic hold that requires no physical engagement
a mechanical latch that holds a door or panel closed until deliberately released
a device that locks using a key or code
n: A positive latching mechanism is a mechanical latch that engages automatically and holds a door closed until it is deliberately released. Fire doors require one. Source: NFPA 80 (Fire Doors – Positive Latching); RA 9514 (Fire Code) RIRR.

q: A color to evoke trustworthiness.
n: Blue is associated with trust, dependability and calm, which is why it is common in corporate and institutional branding. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color Psychology).

q: Which of the following is not considered a vision window?
n: Clerestory windows sit high on the wall, above eye level, to admit daylight and ventilation, not views. Bay, ribbon and awning windows can be vision windows. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Window); Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: Stainless steel cladding is to be introduced to the master bedroom as an accent. Which finish shall be used to achieve the least reflective stainless steel surface?
n: Stainless steel finish No. 2B is a dull, cold-rolled matte finish with the least reflectivity of the choices. No. 4 is brushed, and No. 8 is a mirror finish. Source: ASTM A480 (Stainless Steel Finishes); International Stainless Steel Forum.

q: In an artisanal bedroom interior, which element does not complement the style?
n: Artisanal interiors celebrate handcraft and natural materials: carved wood, woven rattan, vintage textiles. A mass-produced modular table does not belong. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Style); Pile, A History of Interior Design.

q: Which of the following features is least likely to be found in a “quiet luxury" interior space?
n: "Quiet luxury" favors understated quality: fine natural materials, neutral palettes and minimal forms. Ornate gilded mirrors are the opposite of that restraint. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Style and Character); contemporary interior design references.

q: What type of base tile is ideal for hygienic purposes in a typical restaurant kitchen?
n: Coved base tiles curve from floor to wall, leaving no sharp corner where dirt and bacteria collect. Food-safety codes call for them in commercial kitchens. Source: FDA Food Code, Sec. 6-201.13 (Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved); Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Restaurants).

q: What type of door is most suitable for separating a restaurant kitchen from the dining area to allow easy two-way access without using hands?
n: Double-acting (two-way swinging) doors open both ways with a push. Servers can pass between kitchen and dining room with full hands. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Restaurants – Kitchen Doors); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8.

q: What is the primary purpose of a bain marie in a professional kitchen setting?
n: A bain-marie is a hot water bath that keeps cooked food and sauces warm at a gentle, even temperature without overcooking them. Source: Culinary Institute of America, The Professional Chef; FDA Food Code (hot holding).

q: What is the primary purpose of a 3-compartment sink in a restaurant kitchen?
o: to manage grease, wastewater, and solids
to separate meat, seafood, and vegetables
to soak, air dry, and store equipment
to wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils and cookware
n: A three-compartment sink lets ware be washed, rinsed and sanitized in sequence, as food codes require for manual warewashing. Source: FDA Food Code, Sec. 4-301.12 (Manual Warewashing – Sink Compartment Requirements).

q: In which industrial application is the reach envelope most critical to ensure safety and efficiency?
n: The reach envelope, the zone a worker can reach comfortably, is most critical in control panel design. Controls must be within safe, efficient reach to avoid errors and strain. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; ISO 14738 (Anthropometric Requirements for Workstations).

q: In anthropometric design, which percentile is commonly used to accommodate the largest range of users, especially for clearance and safety considerations?
n: Clearances are designed for the 95th percentile, so 95% of users fit. Reaches are designed for the 5th percentile, so the smallest users can reach. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Percentiles).

q: Which field focuses on analyzing human body movements to improve safety and efficiency in physically demanding work environments?
n: Occupational biomechanics analyzes the forces and movements of the body during physical work. It is used to reduce injuries and improve efficiency. Source: Chaffin, Andersson & Martin, Occupational Biomechanics; International Ergonomics Association.

q: What is the standard seat height for bar chair?
n: Bar chairs (stools) for standard 1,000–1,100 mm bars have seats about 700–760 mm high. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Bar Seating); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: In an industrial workspace, what unit is used to measure if the lighting meets the minimum required illumination for tasks like assembly or inspection?
n: Required task illuminance is specified and measured in lux (lumens per sqm) with a light meter. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Illuminance Recommendations); DOLE OSHS Rule 1075 (Illumination).

q: Which of the following is not typically considered part of interior furnishings?
n: A wall mural is a wall finish or artwork applied to the building surface. Area rugs, accent chairs and table lamps are movable furnishings. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furnishings vs. Finishes).

q: Which of the following table types is most closely associated with modernist design principles?
n: The Parsons table, with legs flush with a square apron in one clean block, came from the Parsons School of Design in the 1930s. It embodies modernist simplicity. Source: Pile, A History of Interior Design; Parsons School of Design history.

q: Acid washing is a finishing technique typically used on which of the following materials?
n: Acid washing is a finishing process applied to stone, such as granite and marble, to give a weathered, textured surface. It is also used to etch concrete. Source: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual (Finishes).

q: What is the most common type of faux leather material?
n: PU (polyurethane) leather is the most common faux leather today. It is softer and more breathable than PVC leather. Source: Textile industry references on synthetic leather; ASTM D2208 (Leather Testing).

q: What is the most damaging factor to synthetic leather when it comes to maintenance?
o: occasional use of mild cleaning agents
n: Prolonged direct sunlight (UV and heat) degrades synthetic leather. The coating fades, dries out and cracks. Source: Manufacturers' care guides for PU/PVC upholstery; ASTM D4329 (UV Exposure of Plastics).

q: Which application is a tile with a grip finish best suited for?
n: Tiles with grip (anti-slip) finishes are made for wet exterior floors such as patios, pool decks and ramps. Source: ANSI A137.1 (DCOF slip resistance); Tile Council of North America Handbook.

q: "Salt and pepper” is a common pattern of which floor tile?
n: "Salt and pepper" is the speckled black-and-white look of granite tiles, from mixed light and dark minerals. Source: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual (Granite).

q: Who is responsible to produce the record drawings?
n: The contractor produces record (as-built) drawings that show the work as actually constructed. The architect may review them. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions – Record Drawings); Architect's Guidelines (2016).

q: Where is a pipe sleeve typically required?
n: Pipe sleeves are cast into slabs and walls where pipes pass through. They allow movement and replacement, and penetrations can then be firestopped. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Sleeves); ASTM E814 (Firestop Systems).

q: Which construction method involves creating a reinforced concrete wall by excavating a trench stabilized with slurry before pouring concrete?
n: A slurry (diaphragm) wall is cast in a trench excavated under bentonite slurry, which holds the trench open until concrete is tremied in. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Diaphragm Walls); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3.

q: In prestressed concrete, what method is used to offset or counteract the weight of the structure using the force from tendons?
n: In the load-balancing method of prestressed concrete design, draped tendons exert upward forces that counteract part of the gravity load. Source: Lin & Burns, Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures (Load Balancing); Nawy, Prestressed Concrete.

q: Minimum main rebars for a spiral column.
n: Spirally reinforced columns need at least 6 longitudinal bars. Tied rectangular columns need 4. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 410.7.3.1 (Minimum number of longitudinal bars); ACI 318.

q: What is an ideal task lighting on the kitchen counter?
n: Under-cabinet strip lighting puts light right on the counter without shadows from the user's head. It is the ideal kitchen task lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Residential Kitchen Lighting).

q: Which of the following is considered a safety lighting?
n: Twin-head emergency lamps are battery-backed units that switch on automatically during power failure to light egress paths, so they are safety lighting. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); NFPA 101, Sec. 7.9.

q: Where should a UFO emergency light be installed?
n: UFO-type (round, recessed or surface) emergency lights are installed on the ceiling to spread egress illumination widely. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Outline specifications are a deliverable under what design phase?
n: Outline specifications are part of the Design Development Phase deliverables, together with the developed drawings and the updated cost estimate. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Design Development Phase deliverables.
